## Detailed Findings

#### 1. SST OpenCode todowrite tool restoration MEDIUM (tool, ui, planning, task-breakdown)

- **What**: SST OpenCode PR #56947 (merged 2026-10-19) restores the `todowrite` tool behind an experimental flag `tools.todowrite.enabled: boolean` in user config. Commit title: "feat: restore the todowrite tool behind an experimental flag". Feature: agents can call `todowrite({ todos: [{ content, status, priority }] })` to create/update a task list shown in the TUI sidebar. Use case: complex multi-step features (5+ subtasks) where the agent breaks down "implement user registration" into "add schema", "write API endpoint", "add validation", "write tests", "update docs" and marks each `pending` / `in_progress` / `completed` / `cancelled` as work progresses. TUI shows live progress; user can see which subtask is blocked. Pattern: task-planning UI surface separate from the message log, persisted per session. Experimental flag gates rollout while UX is refined (e.g. where to show the list, how to handle abandoned todos, whether to auto-archive completed lists).

- **Why**: Alexi audit 2026-10-20: `grep -r "todowrite\|todo.*write" src/tool/tools/` returned zero matches. No `src/tool/tools/todowrite.ts` or `src/tool/tools/todo.ts` found. TUI modules (`src/cli/tui/`) do not render task lists (checked `src/cli/tui/Session.tsx`, `src/cli/tui/App.tsx`, no todo-list component found). Feature gap: Alexi agents handle complex multi-step tasks but have no structured planning surface — all subtask communication happens inline in message history, which is hard to scan for "which of 8 subtasks are done?". Adding todowrite improves observability (user sees progress at a glance without re-reading 50 turns) and agent discipline (explicit todo update forces agent to acknowledge completion before moving to next step). MEDIUM priority, ~8-12h implementation (add tool definition with Zod schema `{ todos: [{ content: string, status: 'pending' | 'in_progress' | 'completed' | 'cancelled', priority: 'high' | 'medium' | 'low' }] }`, persist todo list in session state, add TUI component to render list in sidebar or below session header, add experimental flag to config, add tests). Scope: CLI-only TUI component (Alexi does not have VS Code extension), behind `experimental.todowrite` config flag matching SST pattern. Size estimate assumes Alexi TUI is Ink-based (confirmed `src/cli/tui/` uses Ink + React 19 from AGENTS.md), so rendering logic is React component.

- **Source**: https://github.com/sst/opencode/pull/56947 (todowrite tool restoration upstream), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/tool/tools/ (no todowrite.ts found), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/cli/tui/ (no todo-list component found)

- **Category**: tool

- **Size**: MEDIUM ~8-12h (add todowrite tool definition with Zod schema for `{ todos: [{ content: string, status: enum, priority: enum }] }`, persist todo list in session state, add Ink React component to TUI sidebar/header to render todo list, add `experimental.todowrite` config flag, write unit tests for tool + TUI component, integration test for todo persistence across session resume)

#### 2. Kilocode subagent edit-tool inheritance CLI-ACTIONABLE MEDIUM (permission, subagent, task, policy)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #15254 (merged 2026-10-19) fixes subagent edit-tool removal on allowlist callers. Commit title: "fix(cli): keep edit tools for subagents of allowlist callers". Issue: a caller whose edit policy is a catch-all deny followed by path-specific allows (e.g. `{ tools: ['edit'], decision: 'deny', priority: 10 }` + `{ tools: ['edit'], paths: ['src/**'], decision: 'allow', priority: 20 }`) had that shape flattened into a blanket edit deny on every delegated child session. `Permission.disabled` then removed `edit`, `write`, and `apply_patch` from the child's tool list, so subagents launched from such a primary agent failed with "Model tried to call unavailable tool 'write'". Fix: treat that shape as an allowlist baseline — writable callers now inherit only their specific denies, and the subagent's own policy governs. Read-only callers (plan mode, `ask` tool, orchestrator, or a user-level deny-all) keep the hard ceiling. Resuming a child created before this change drops the stale catch-all deny when the fresh ceiling no longer reproduces it. Pattern: subagent permission inheritance must preserve allowlist structure instead of flattening to most-restrictive decision.

- **Why**: Alexi audit needed 2026-10-20: `src/tool/task.ts` (subagent delegation, 600+ lines, likely contains child-session spawning logic), `src/permission/index.ts` (policy inheritance, 1110 lines, `PermissionManager` class with `getRules()` / `addRule()` / `updateRule()` methods), `src/permission/agent-manager.ts` (agent-manager-specific permission handling). Grep for `permission.*inherit|policy.*child|subagent.*permission|task.*permission` found zero matches in `src/permission/` or `src/tool/task.ts` (searched full paths). Potential gap: if Alexi subagent delegation flattens allowlist shape the same way Kilo did pre-fix (take most-restrictive decision from parent policy without preserving path-specific allows), Alexi will hit the same "Model tried to call unavailable tool 'write'" failure when a plan-mode or allowlist-primary session delegates a child. MEDIUM priority CLI-ACTIONABLE: (1) reproduce by creating a session with catch-all edit deny + path-specific allow, (2) delegate a subagent via task tool, (3) check if subagent can write to allowed paths. If subagent fails, port Kilo fix: preserve allowlist structure in `src/tool/task.ts` child-session construction, pass only specific parent denies (not catch-all deny) to child's `PermissionManager`, let child's own policy govern. Estimate ~6-8h (audit task.ts delegation logic, add unit tests for allowlist inheritance, port fix if gap confirmed, integration test for writable subagent from allowlist parent).

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/15254 (subagent edit-tool inheritance fix upstream), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/tool/task.ts (subagent delegation, audit needed), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/permission/index.ts (policy inheritance, audit needed)

- **Category**: config

- **Size**: MEDIUM ~6-8h (audit subagent delegation logic in src/tool/task.ts, reproduce allowlist-parent + writable-child scenario, add unit tests for permission inheritance with catch-all deny + path allows, port Kilo fix if gap confirmed, integration test for writable subagent from allowlist parent)

#### 3. Kilocode custom auto router REFERENCE-ONLY (routing, cloud, eval, cost-optimization)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #15183 (merged 2026-10-19) implements custom auto-routing with client models and local evals. Commit title: "feat(cli): custom auto routers with client models and local evals". Feature: `kilo-auto/custom/<slug>` model type that asks `https://auto-routing.kiloapps.io/v1/decide` for routing decision, then dispatches the picked entry (local provider for client picks, gateway with `x-kilo-auto-decision` header for gateway picks). `kilo auto router add|remove|list` registers client entries from CLI's resolved model metadata. `kilo auto eval` runs missing client evals in cached `node:22-slim` Docker container with host CLI version, one fresh container per case, credentials through 0600 env file, uploads each result immediately. Pattern: cost-aware routing with custom decision service, eval-driven quality verification before adding models to router pool.

- **Why**: Alexi is CLI-only with SAP AI Core backend. No Kilo Cloud integration, no `https://auto-routing.kiloapps.io` endpoint. Alexi routing is JSON-driven via `routing-config.json` with static model-to-deployment-id mapping (`src/core/router.ts`). REFERENCE-ONLY: if Alexi adds enterprise routing service (cost-optimized model selection, eval-driven quality gates, multi-tenant routing policies), reference this pattern: (1) custom decision service with HTTP contract (`POST /v1/decide` with session context + available models, returns `{ model, provider }` pick), (2) client-side eval runner (Docker container per eval case, credential isolation, immediate upload), (3) CLI commands for router pool management (`alexi router add|remove|list`). Pattern not applicable to current Alexi setup (SAP AI Core catalog is static per resource group, no cross-tenant routing, no eval service). Priority SKIP unless/until Alexi adds cloud orchestration tier.

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/15183 (custom auto router upstream), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/router.ts (static JSON-driven routing, no cloud decision service), docs/ROUTING.md (routing architecture, static config only)

- **Category**: N/A (routing, cloud, eval, cost-optimization, reference-only)

- **Size**: SKIP. Alexi CLI-only with static routing-config.json, no Kilo Cloud integration. Pattern reference for future enterprise routing service.

#### 4. Kilocode browser permission persistence REFERENCE-ONLY (vscode, permission, browser, extension)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #15235 (merged 2026-10-19) lets `browser_open` permissions be allowed always in VS Code extension. Commit title: "fix(vscode): let browser_open permissions be allowed always". Issue: VS Code extension state did not persist "allow always" checkbox for `browser_open` tool, so user had to re-approve every session. Fix: store `browser_open` allowlist in VS Code extension `globalState` (keyed by host pattern or `*` for all), check on tool call, skip permission prompt when matched. Pattern: extension-state persistence for low-risk tools (browser open to docs / localhost preview) to reduce approval fatigue.

- **Why**: Alexi is CLI-only with no VS Code extension, JetBrains plugin, or desktop app. `src/tool/tools/browser.ts` exists (checked 2026-10-20, 13699 bytes, implements `browser_open` tool with `xdg-open` / `open` / `start` dispatch). Permission prompt logic in `src/permission/prompt.ts` (10060 bytes) but no VS Code `globalState` equivalent (Alexi CLI stores permissions in `~/.alexi/` file-based config, not extension state). REFERENCE-ONLY: if Alexi adds VS Code extension, reference this pattern for low-risk tool allowlists: (1) store allowlist in extension `globalState` (keyed by host or `*`), (2) check on tool call before permission prompt, (3) add UI checkbox "allow always for <host>" or "allow always for all hosts". Current priority SKIP — Alexi CLI permission system already supports "allow" decision in `routing-config.json` or session rules, which persists across sessions without extension state. VS Code-specific persistence not needed.

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/15235 (browser permission persistence upstream), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/tool/tools/browser.ts (browser_open tool exists, CLI-only xdg-open/open/start dispatch), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/permission/prompt.ts (permission prompt logic, no VS Code globalState)

- **Category**: N/A (vscode, permission, browser, extension, reference-only)

- **Size**: SKIP. Alexi CLI-only, no VS Code extension. Pattern reference for future extension: store allowlist in globalState, check before prompt.

#### 5. Cline Windows build fixes REFERENCE-ONLY (windows, build, rmSync, mkdtempSync)

- **What**: Cline PR #15206 (merged 2026-10-19) makes `build:platforms:single` work on Windows. Commit title: "fix(cli): make build:platforms:single work on Windows". Issue: build scripts used shell `rm -rf` which fails on Windows without bash. Fix: replace with `fs.rmSync({ recursive: true, force: true, maxRetries: 3, retryDelay: 100 })` in `apps/cli/script/build.ts`, retry smoke-test directory cleanup while detached hub process exits on Windows, use `fs.mkdtempSync` with non-Windows `fs.chmodSync` in `apps/cli/script/compile-binary.ts`. Pattern: cross-platform build scripts use Node.js fs APIs instead of shell commands.

- **Why**: Alexi does not ship compiled binaries. NPM-only distribution (`npm install -g @alexi/cli` or `npm link` for dev). No `compile-binary.ts` or platform-specific build scripts found (`ls scripts/` returned zero matches, `package.json` has no `build:platforms` script). REFERENCE-ONLY: if Alexi adds binary compilation (e.g. `pkg`, `nexe`, `esbuild` standalone, or `bun build --compile`), reference this pattern for Windows compatibility: (1) use `fs.rmSync` instead of shell `rm -rf`, (2) retry cleanup with `maxRetries`/`retryDelay` on Windows to handle detached-process file locks, (3) use `fs.mkdtempSync` + conditional `chmodSync` (Windows does not honor Unix modes). Current priority SKIP — Alexi build is `tsc -p tsconfig.json` to `dist/`, no platform-specific binaries.

- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/15206 (Windows build fixes upstream), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/package.json (no build:platforms script), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/scripts/ (no compile-binary.ts found)

- **Category**: N/A (windows, build, rmSync, mkdtempSync, reference-only)

- **Size**: SKIP. Alexi NPM-only distribution, no compiled binaries. Pattern reference for future binary compilation on Windows.

#### 6. Cline skills CLI pin REFERENCE-ONLY (skills, marketplace, dependabot, version-pinning)

- **What**: Cline PR #15144 (merged 2026-10-19) pins the skills CLI release as an exact devDependency. Commit title: "chore: pin the skills CLI release and let Dependabot bump it". Issue: `npx skills@latest` in `cline skill` command and marketplace fallback ran the latest Vercel release, which could change behavior or raise Node floor under shipped builds without any Cline change (1.5.16 broke Node 18/20 on 2026-07-10, 1.5.19 raised floor to `>=22.20` on 2026-07-16). Fix: add `skills@<exact-version>` as devDependency of `@cline/core`, expose as `SKILLS_CLI_PACKAGE` constant, run `npx ${SKILLS_CLI_PACKAGE}` instead of `npx skills@latest`. Dependabot opens PR for each new version so bumps go through CI + review. Package code is never executed by Cline; only `package.json` version is read at build time. Pattern: pin external CLI tools as devDependencies with Dependabot auto-bump, avoid `@latest` in production code.

- **Why**: Alexi does not integrate Cline skills marketplace. No `src/skill/marketplace.ts` or `npx skills` invocations found (`grep -r "npx skills\|skills@latest" src/` returned zero matches). Alexi skill system (`src/skill/`) is file-based (load from `~/.alexi/skills/` or project `.alexi/skills/`), not Vercel marketplace. REFERENCE-ONLY: if Alexi adds external CLI tool dependencies (e.g. MCP registry CLI, SAP AI Core deployment CLI, npm package scanner), reference this pattern: (1) add tool as exact devDependency (e.g. `"@sap/ai-core-cli": "1.2.3"`), (2) expose version as constant (`export const SAP_CLI_PACKAGE = '@sap/ai-core-cli@1.2.3'`), (3) run `npx ${SAP_CLI_PACKAGE}` instead of `npx @sap/ai-core-cli@latest`, (4) configure Dependabot to auto-bump (add to `.github/dependabot.yml`). Current priority SKIP — Alexi does not invoke external CLI tools via npx in production code.

- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/15144 (skills CLI pin upstream), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/skill/ (file-based skill system, no marketplace integration), grep results (no npx skills invocations found)

- **Category**: N/A (skills, marketplace, dependabot, version-pinning, reference-only)

- **Size**: SKIP. Alexi does not integrate Cline skills marketplace or invoke external CLI tools via npx. Pattern reference for future external CLI dependencies.
